# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-29 (Extended v197)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Champs-Élysées, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby.

Paris sewer system: extensive network (5,300 fathoms in 1663; 40,300 metres by 1 January 1832). Contemporary sections use porous stone filled with mortar on concrete foundation (200 francs per metre). Follows line of streets above (2,200 streets). Ridge divides waters—some flow to Seine, others to Grand Sewer. Sainte-Avoye sewer marks watershed culmination. Network includes Rue Saint-Denis gallery, Cadran gallery with three blind alleys, belt sewer, Montmartre sewer with "crossroads de service" (later suppressed). Grand Sewer (old brook of Ménilmontant) terminates in blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant knoll. No direct communication with branch collecting Paris waters beginning Quartier Popincourt falling into Seine through Amelot sewer above Isle Louviers. Belt sewer has no two outlets as popularly believed. **Fontis phenomenon**: Water filters into friable subjacent strata; footway (flagstones in ancient sewers, cement on concrete in new galleries) lacks underpinning and gives way. Fold in flooring causes crack and crumbling. Soaked soil in state of fusion—neither earth nor water. Depth varies: some fontis 3-4 feet deep, others 8-10 feet, some unfathomable. In Lunière fontis, man takes day to disappear; in Philippeaux slough, five minutes. Density determines safety—child escapes where man perishes. First law: discard all loads. Death therein slow if earth predominates, prompt if water predominates—swallowing in mire, asphyxiation by filth, sulfuretted hydrogen, humiliating and infamous. **Champs-Élysées quagmire**: Common in subsoil; difficult to handle in hydraulic works; excessive fluidity. In 1836, reconstruction of old stone sewer beneath Faubourg Saint-Honoré (where Valjean currently is) lasted nearly six months due to quicksand obstacle; operation lasted with four months and half of rain and three Seine floods. **Beautreillis sewer incident**: Young Vicomte d'Escoubleau drowned escaping Duke of Sourdis; Duchess de Sourdis, informed of death, forgot to weep through sniffing salts.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate lodgings. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work, moved there (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate lodgings (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest (Chapter 28). Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there thereafter (Chapter 28). Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7, Chapter 28). Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month (Chapter 28). Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven (Chapter 28). Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford (Chapter 28). **Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate (Chapter 29)**.

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with Cosette memory. **Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Barricade, Sewer Escape, and Emergence (Chapters 24-29)

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar; grief surpassed bounds.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman and officer, smashed helmet. Stared silently. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting, caring. Reappeared in intervals. Nothing resembling blow or personal defence from his hands. Held peace, lent succor. Received few scratches only. Meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: After final collapse, Valjean found himself trapped behind small wall near Rue de la Petite Truanderie. Discovered iron grating about two feet square beneath loose paving-stones, leading to dark aperture. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted inert Marius onto shoulders, descended into well with elbows and knees three metres below surface, dropped grating behind. Executed with strength of giant and rapidity of eagle.

**Sewer journey (6th June, after barricade)**: Escaped via Paris sewer system. Transition from daylight to obscurity, midday to midnight, tumult to silence. Blindness, deafness. Cautiously advanced, fearing hole/sink/gulf; discovered paving continued. Gust of fetidness informed him of place. After fifty paces, passage terminated; two ways presented. Chose based on slope leading to river. Thought probably in sewer des Halles; better to plunge into labyrinth than risk daylight capture between Pont au Change and Pont-Neuf. **Water flow changed direction**: Gradually perceived water of rivulet beating against heels instead of toes. Sewer began descending toward belt sewer, not Seine. Ridge forms watershed; Valjean reached culminating point, directed course toward belt sewer. **Branch encounters**: Every encounter with branch felt its angles; avoided narrower ways terminating in blind alleys, correctly judging by physical sense. Avoided quadruple trap—four labyrinths set in darkness. **Police patrol (6th June)**: Prefect Gisquet ordered battue of sewers. Three squads explored subterranean drain. One patrol explored curving gallery and three blind alleys beneath Rue du Cadran. While passing lantern, Valjean perceived entrance to gallery narrower than principal passage, did not penetrate, passed on. Patrol, emerging from Cadran gallery, fancied they heard footsteps in direction of belt sewer—actually Valjean's steps. Sergeant raised lantern, squad gazed into mist. Light and shadow mingled with darkness very far off. Valjean hugged wall and halted. Lack of sleep, food, emotions caused him pass into state of visionary. **Patrol's decision**: At crossroads "de service" in Montmartre sewer, patrol whispered together. Concluded they had been mistaken, no noise, useless to entangle in belt sewer, ought hasten toward Saint-Merry; if anything to do, in that quarter. Patrol resumed march, leaving Valjean behind. **Sergeant's discharge**: Before departure, sergeant discharged gun in direction of Valjean. Detonation rolled from echo to echo in crypt. Plaster fell into stream, ball struck arch over his head. Had patrol not been forbidden to separate by prefecture instructions, Jean Valjean would have been captured.

**Emergence to Seine (6th June, after patrol departure)**: Valjean and Marius continued toward belt sewer and downward toward Seine. At point where Montmartre sewer joins Grand Sewer, four ways presented; Valjean selected broadest—belt sewer. Descended toward Seine. **Critical sewer knowledge**: Grand Sewer terminates in blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant. No direct communication with branch falling into Seine through Amelot sewer. Had Valjean ascended, would have become lost at wall in gloom. **Emergence to quay**: Valjean and Marius approached inclined plane on quay descended to shore. **Authority presence**: Man in buttoned-up coat walked to extremity of shore, remained in thought, fists clenched, eyes searching. Perceived large iron grating, low, arched, garnished with heavy lock and three massive hinges at point where land ended and water began. Grating—sort of door pierced at base of quay—opened on river and shore. Blackish stream passed under it, discharged into Seine. **Grating significance**: Grating had just been opened (no sound heard—singular circumstance). Man before whom door opened had key not hook. **Hackney-coach surveillance**: Buttoned-up man made sign to passing empty hackney-coach on quay. Driver understood, recognized person with whom to deal, turned about, began following two men at top of quay at foot-pace. Not observed by slouching, tattered personage in advance. **Coachman's preparations**: Coachman, foreseeing prolonged wait, encased horses' muzzles in damp oat bag. Rare passers-by on Pont de Jéna turned heads momentarily at two motionless items in landscape—man on shore, carriage on quay. **Valjean's knowledge and ignorance**: Valjean knows nothing of sewer's "frightful drain" and its ramifications. By retracing steps, could potentially reach Amelot sewer via Filles-du-Calvaire passage, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery; thence to outlet near Arsenal. But would require thorough familiarity he lacks. **Marius's address**: Jean Valjean read address "Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, number 6, Monsieur Gillenormand" from pocketbook in light of air-hole. Remained absorbed in thought, repeating address in low tone. Replaced pocketbook in Marius' pocket. **Valjean's recovery and continuation**: After eating, strength returned. Took Marius up once more upon back, placed latter's head carefully on right shoulder, resumed descent of sewer. **Continuing journey conditions**: Only growing pallor of pools of light indicated sun withdrawing from pavement, day ending. Rolling of vehicles overhead becoming intermittent then ceasing indicated approach to solitary region near outer boulevards or extreme outer quays.

**Fontis encounter (Chapter 29)**: Caused by downpour preceding day. Pavement, badly sustained by subjacent sand, gave way, produced stoppage of water. Infiltration took place, slip followed. Dislocated bottom sank into ooze. Valjean felt pavement vanishing beneath feet, entered slime. Water on surface, slime at bottom. Could not retrace steps—Marius dying, Jean Valjean exhausted. Feet plunged progressively deeper: slime to calves then knees, water to knees then waist then arm-pits. Dense mire, support and obstacle simultaneously. Marius and Valjean would have singly stood chance of extricating themselves; together, mud could not uphold both. Valjean held Marius on high with unheard-of expenditure of force. Sank until only head above water, two arms holding up Marius. Turned face rearward to escape water, breathe. Became like mother in old paintings of deluge holding child. Kicked foot forward desperately, struck something solid at supreme moment—point of support. **The solid point**: Beginning of other watershed of pavement, bent but not given way, curved under water like plank in single piece. Well built pavements form vault, possess firmness. Fragment of vaulting, partly submerged but solid, veritable inclined plane. Once on this plane, he was safe. Valjean mounted inclined plane, reached other side of quagmire.

**Post-fontis state and continuation**: Although had not left life in fontis, seemed to have left strength behind. Supreme effort exhausted him. Lassitude such that obliged to pause for breath every three or four steps, lean against wall. Once forced to seat himself on banquette to alter Marius' position, thought he should remain there. But vigor dead, energy not. Rose again. Walked on desperately, almost fast, proceeded hundred paces almost without drawing breath, suddenly came in contact with wall. Reached elbow of sewer, arriving at turn with head bent down, struck wall. Raised eyes, at extremity of vault, far, very far away in front, perceived light. Not terrible light—good, white light. Daylight. Jean Valjean saw the outlet.

## Year 8 (Spring) Seasonal Observations

Rain threatened since morning but held off. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Baker's boy late again, line at oven grew long. Light went early, as that time of year. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs. Kassa complained of aching back, as usual. Kassa counted coins twice, still came up penny short. Vesmira Thornmere and Taric Corrley talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse. Taric told Kassa "You look tired"; Kassa did not deny. "Price of salt is scandal," said Taric. "A scandal," agreed Kassa Stenson.
